extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (practitioners engaged in USPTO patent prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting requirements for interviews, models/exhibits, and amendments during USPTO patent prosecution (including timing, form, signature, responsiveness, and reexamination-specific rules). Covers 37 CFR 1.121, 1.111, 1.91, 1.312, and related MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model/exhibit handling (37 CFR 1.91 vs demonstration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model received by the examiner from the applicant or attorney which complies with 37 CFR 1.91 and which is made part of the application record must be properly recorded on the 'Contents' portion of the application file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a model or exhibit is merely used for demonstration and is not made part of the record (does not comply with 37 CFR 1.91), a full description of what was demonstrated/exhibited must be made of record in the application (see 37 CFR 1.133(b)). Demonstrations of apparatus or exhibits too large to be brought into the Office may be viewed by the examiner outside the Office (Washington, D.C. area) with supervisory patent examiner approval; such viewing is presumed essential to developing and clarifying the issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview after final rejection — one interview normally permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, one interview after final rejection is permitted; prior to the interview the intended purpose and content should be presented briefly, preferably in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview may be granted if the examiner is convinced that disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration. Interviews merely to restate arguments of record or to discuss new limitations which would require more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied. See MPEP § 714.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits for interviews after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be held after the expiration of the shortened statutory period and prior to the maximum permitted statutory period of 6 months without an extension of time (see MPEP § 706.07(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A second or further interview after a final rejection may be held if the examiner is convinced it will expedite issues for appeal or disposal of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-filing/interviews under 37 CFR 1.312 (interviews after allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is sent to issue it is technically no longer under the primary examiner's jurisdiction (37 CFR 1.312); an interview involving detailed consideration of claims sought to be entered and discussion of prior art for determining allowability should not be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for interviews on cases where a notice of allowance has been mailed should be granted only with specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a written showing of extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must be made by paper complying with 37 CFR 1.52 (37 CFR 1.121 general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in applications (other than reissue) are made by filing a paper, in compliance with § 1.52, directing that specified amendments be made (37 CFR 1.121).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline procedural requirement for all non-reissue amendment submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment by instruction to delete/replace/add paragraph (specification amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: To amend the specification (other than claims), submit an instruction which unambiguously identifies the location to delete one or more paragraphs, replace a deleted paragraph with replacement paragraph(s), or add paragraph(s); include replacement/added paragraph(s) in clean form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate marked-up version of any replacement paragraph(s) must accompany the amendment on pages separate from the clean replacement, showing all changes relative to the previous version (brackets for deletions, underlining for additions, or equivalent). A marked-up version is not required for a newly added paragraph or a deleted paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment by replacement section (when section headings used)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification contains section headings, amendments may be made by submitting a reference to the section heading with instruction to delete and replace that section, a replacement section in clean form, and a separate marked-up version showing changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up version must show all changes relative to the previous version; changes may use brackets/underlining or equivalent marking systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment by substitute specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification (other than claims) may be amended by submitting an instruction to replace the specification, a substitute specification in compliance with § 1.125(b), and a separate marked-up version showing all changes relative to the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute specifications require compliance with § 1.125(b); marked-up version aids examiner review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of previously deleted matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Deleted matter may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously deleted matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direction by applicant to remove a previously entered amendment will not be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment format — rewriting and clean form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a claim must be made by rewriting such claim with all changes included; the rewriting is construed as cancelling the previous version. Any rewritten or newly added claim must be in clean form (no markings) and be accompanied by a marked-up version separate from the amendment showing all changes relative to the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A parenthetical expression should follow the claim number indicating status (e.g., 'amended', 'twice amended', 'new') in both the clean and marked-up versions. Marked-up versions need not be supplied for added or canceled claims; if supplied, identify any added or canceled claims in the marked-up version (e.g., 'Claim 6 has been canceled').

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of canceled claim requires new claim number
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim canceled by amendment (deleted in its entirety) may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats canceled claims as removed; reinstatement is effective only by creating a new numbered claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting a clean version of entire set of pending claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A clean version of the entire set of pending claims may be submitted in a single amendment paper; such submission is construed as directing the cancellation of all previous versions of any pending claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up version is required only for claims being changed by the current amendment. Any claim not accompanied by a marked-up version will be treated as asserted unchanged relative to the immediate prior version. Parenthetical expressions from previous versions should not appear in the clean set except when a claim is being amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to application drawings must be submitted on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Upon approval by the examiner, new drawings in compliance with § 1.84 including the changes must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed drawing changes should be clearly identified in red on a separate paper to facilitate examiner review and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require amendments to ensure internal consistency across claims, spec, and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict bar: amendments may not add subject matter beyond the original disclosure; reinstatement of deleted matter limited as described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for examiner's amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, including the claims, made by the Office in an examiner's amendment may be made by specific instructions to insert or delete subject matter set forth in the examiner's amendment; compliance with paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2) or (c)(1) of § 1.121 is not required for such examiner's amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1302.04 for procedures—examiner's amendments are an Office-initiated exception to clean/marked-up replacement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special amendment rules for reissue and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in reissue applications must be made in accordance with § 1.173. Amendments to patents in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with § 1.530(d)-(j). In patent-owner-filed reexaminations, the patent owner may amend at the time of the request in accordance with 37 CFR 1.510(e). No amendment/response can be filed between the date of the request for reexamination and the order for reexamination (37 CFR 1.530(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following the order for reexamination and prior to examination phase, an amendment may be filed only with the patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530(b). During the examination phase, amendments may be filed after the first examination (37 CFR 1.112), after final rejection or appeal if meeting 1.116, and when specifically required by the examiner. See MPEP §§ 2250, 2266, and 714.12 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and authority requirement for amendments (37 CFR 1.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment must be signed by a person having authority to prosecute the application. An unsigned or improperly signed amendment will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable signatories include: (1) registered attorney or agent of record appointed per § 1.34(b); (2) registered attorney or agent not of record acting under § 1.34(a); (3) an assignee as provided under § 3.71(b); or (4) all of the applicants (§ 1.41(b)) unless entire interest assigned. If unsigned/improperly signed, the amendment will be listed but not entered; applicant given a 1-month period to ratify (37 CFR 1.135(c)). Form paragraph 7.84.01 may be used. Amendments signed by persons removed from register under 37 CFR 10.11 are not entered and are submitted to Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment signed by applicant when attorney of record exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment signed by the applicant is received in an application where a duly appointed attorney or agent exists, the amendment should be entered and acted upon; two copies of the action should be prepared—one to the attorney and one directly to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include notation 'Copy to applicant' on original and both copies. Attention should be called to 37 CFR 1.33(a) or 1.33(c) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment timing and status (37 CFR 1.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment is received on or before the mail date of the first Office action under 37 CFR 1.104 (37 CFR 1.115(a)). A preliminary amendment not filed along with the original application does not enjoy the status of part of the original disclosure except in specific limited circumstances (e.g., certain 1.53(b) filings without oath).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments should accompany the application or be filed after the application has its application number and filing date. An amendment canceling claims to reduce filing fee should be filed with the application. A preliminary amendment may be disapproved by the Commissioner if it unduly interferes with the preparation of an Office action (37 CFR 1.115(b)). If non-compliant with 1.121, the LIE will send a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment with a 30-day/one-month time limit and no extensions; failure to comply results in examination without entry of the preliminary amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must be fully responsive to a non-final Office action (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office action after the first examination is adverse in any respect, the applicant must reply and request reconsideration or further examination. To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the reply must be reduced to writing which distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors in the examiner's action and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. The reply must appear throughout to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifically pointing out how the claims patentably distinguish them from the references does not comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply must show patentable novelty and avoidance of references
rubrics_metrics.description: In amending in reply to a rejection of claims, the applicant must clearly point out the patentable novelty believed to be present and show how the amendments avoid cited references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting arguments in support of new claims and amendments, 37 CFR 1.111(b) must be complied with by pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal vs merits matters and completeness of reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reply to a requirement is necessary to further consideration of the claims, or where allowable subject matter has been indicated, a complete reply must either comply with formal requirements or specifically traverse each one not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawing and specification corrections, presentation of a new oath, etc., are generally formal matters. The line between formal matters and merits is not sharp; examiners may insist on formal corrections prior to indicating allowable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up & clean-version requirement for post-March-1-2001 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: After March 1, 2001, all amendments to the specification, including the claims, must be made by replacement paragraph/section/claim in clean form (without underlining/bracketing) and accompanied by a marked-up version showing changes relative to the immediate previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice eliminates the need for Office handwriting/red ink and hard-to-scan markings. The marked-up version is an aid to the examiner. 'Previous version' means the version of record in the application as originally filed or from a previously entered amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment treatment and Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121, the Office will notify applicant by a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment and give a time period to comply. For preliminary amendments the LIE sets a 30-day/one-month time limit with no extensions; for amendments after a non-final Office action the LIE sets a 30-day/one-month time limit with extensions allowed under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Failure to reply may result in examination without entry or abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.22 for treatment of non-compliant amendments after final rejection. The LIE handles notification and time periods; failure to respond timely to the Notice can have severe consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of amendments not fully responsive to non-final action
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may treat an amendment not fully responsive by: (A) accepting the amendment as adequate reply to avoid abandonment (35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.135); (B) notifying the applicant that the reply must be completed within the remaining period for reply to avoid abandonment; or (C) setting a new time period for applicant to complete the reply pursuant to 37 CFR 1.135(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment depends on whether the amendment is bona fide, whether sufficient time remains to file a completed reply, and the nature of the deficiency. If amendment substantially responds but contains a minor deficiency, examiner may act and issue a new Office action reiterating the unaddressed rejection. For serious omissions, notify to supply omission within remaining time if sufficient; if insufficient time, set a 1-month time to complete reply and do not further examine on merits until omission is timely supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or subsequent supplemental reply entry/disapproval factors
rubrics_metrics.description: A second (or subsequent) supplemental reply will be entered unless disapproved by the Commissioner. A second (or subsequent) supplemental reply may be disapproved if it unduly interferes with an Office action being prepared in response to the previous reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors considered in disapproving include: (i) the state of preparation of an Office action responsive to the previous reply as of the date of receipt of the supplemental reply; and (ii) the nature of any changes to the specification or claims that would result from entry of the supplemental reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone notification and interview-summary when omission notification given by phone
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant is notified by telephone that an omission must be supplied within the remaining time for reply, an interview summary record must be completed and entered into the application file to provide a record of such notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When telephone notification is not possible, notify the applicant in an Office communication that the omission must be supplied within the remaining time period for reply. Example context: amendment filed shortly after Office action where it's apparent amendment was not filed in reply.
